name: Susu (Soso)
notes: Susu (Soso), Central Mande (Susu-Yalunka branch), spoken by ~2.4 million people mainly in coastal Guinea, with communities in Sierra Leone and Guinea-Bissau. Written with the Guinean national-languages Latin alphabet (post-1988 reform), the same convention used for the Bambara (bm) spec in this repo: IPA-style letters ɛ, ɔ, ɲ, ŋ are used directly rather than digraphs, ⟨y⟩ = /j/, and the labial-velar stop is ⟨gb⟩ = /ɡb/. Fourteen oral vowel phonemes (7 qualities x length) are attested; length is written by doubling the vowel letter, following the same convention as ff/wo/bm. Susu also has a full set of nasalized vowel counterparts (ĩ ũ ẽ õ ɛ̃ ɔ̃ ã), attested phonemically by the cited Wikipedia phoneme table, but the source consulted does not state how nasalization is marked in the standard orthography (nasal-vowel diacritic vs. a following ⟨n⟩), so no nasal-vowel graphemes are asserted here — recording an unconfirmed spelling convention would be a fabrication (AGENTS.md §4). Prenasalized ⟨nd⟩ and ⟨ng⟩ are attested directly as phonemes /nd/ and /ŋɡ/ in the same table. This spec is quality:research pending a primary-source, letter-by-letter cross-check of the orthography table.
